messages.subject: Execution halted warnings
parts:

Loading required package: methods

1: In max(IRanges::end(g.meth[seqnames(g.meth) == chrs[i], ])) :
  no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
2: In is(seqnames, "Rle") : NAs introduced by coercion
Execution halted

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Execution halted warnings
parts:
You can try to use the development version, but I don't think it will help. What experiment are you running? RRBS or WGBS ? updating to development version might help with memory. Also, removing intermediate objects such as methylRawList will help with the memory.

But I can't tell you where this specific error is coming from without more information, I guess nobody can. You are not even sharing the most basic information: which functions are you running and which one of them gives the error. Please see the link above if you need more help, without a reproducible example, it is difficult to find what is going wrong, it has to do something with GRanges objects, but many functions use those objects.

Best,
Altuna

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Execution halted warnings
parts: Sorry for not understanding what you need.  I was just trying to get the data through filtering and unite and with a data set this large, I needed to run a script through the server.  So, i was unable to tell exactly which function was spitting out the error. I did finally get it to run.  There were some memory issues on our server that I adjusted my submission script for and it ran beautifully.

On Fri, Jul 18, 2014 at 2:21 PM, Altuna Akalin <aak...@gmail.com> wrote:
You can try to use the development version, but I don't think it will help. What experiment are you running? RRBS or WGBS ? updating to development version might help with memory. Also, removing intermediate objects such as methylRawList will help with the memory.

But I can't tell you where this specific error is coming from without more information, I guess nobody can. You are not even sharing the most basic information: which functions are you running and which one of them gives the error. Please see the link above if you need more help, without a reproducible example, it is difficult to find what is going wrong, it has to do something with GRanges objects, but many functions use those objects.

Best,
Altuna
